title: Annotated call graph (owned by Epic B, consumed by Epic C)
description: Kernel call graph rooted at sched_ext kfuncs. Each node is one kernel function (inlined helpers are their own nodes, reached through the call site that inlined them) annotated with the struct fields it reads/writes and an ordered list of events (locks, assertions, atomics, writes, errors, guards, calls). Line numbers refer to the kernel tree at kernel_commit. Consumers must treat anything not stated here as unknown: an absent event list or missing kinds of events are not evidence of absence.

kernel_version.description: Kernel tag the graph describes (KERNEL_VERSION). Fixtures carry the value of the catalog fixture they are tested with.

kernel_commit.description: Full commit SHA of the analysed kernel tree. Every file/line in the graph refers to this commit.

generator.description: Tool + version that produced the graph, or 'hand-written' for fixtures

illustrative.description: true for hand-written fixtures. Their facts are taken from the source by hand and are not an extraction result: consumers must not treat them as verified kernel facts.

roots.description: kfunc names the traversal started from; each must be a key of nodes

fieldref.description: struct.field[.subfield], named by the outermost tracked struct, e.g. task_struct.scx.ops_state (sched_ext_entity is reached as task_struct.scx), rq.scx.flags (scx_rq as rq.scx), scx_dispatch_q.nr

kind.description: kfunc = a registered sched_ext kfunc; internal = expanded kernel function; boundary = recorded (file/line known) but not expanded, because of the depth limit or a subsystem boundary; external = no definition in the analysed IR (out-of-line in another object, e.g. _raw_spin_lock, irq_work_queue). boundary and external nodes have no events and their effects are unknown.

file.description: Source file relative to the kernel root, e.g. kernel/sched/ext.c

end_line.description: Last line of the definition (closing brace); every event line of the node lies in [line, end_line]

depth.description: Shortest call distance from any root (roots are 0)

reads.description: Tracked fields read anywhere in the body (set, unordered)

writes.description: Tracked fields written anywhere in the body (set, unordered). Every entry also appears as a write or atomic event when events are present.

events.description: In program order. Absent = not extracted (unknown), [] = extracted and empty.

callees.description: One entry per call site. Every callee also appears as a call event when events are present. Lock, unlock and lockdep-assertion helpers appear as lock/unlock/assert_* events instead of callees.

target.description: Function name (a key of nodes), or for kind=indirect the ops/method slot, e.g. ops.dispatch or sched_class.enqueue_task

kind.description: indirect = call through a function pointer (SCX_CALL_OP* into BPF, sched_class methods); never dropped even when unresolved

lock/unlock = acquire/release of the lock named by 'lock'; assert_held/assert_not_held = lockdep_assert_*() (CONFIG_LOCKDEP only, checks but never acquires); atomic = atomic_*/cmpxchg/set_bit on 'field'; write = plain store (incl. WRITE_ONCE, list/rbtree linkage) to 'field'; error = scx_error()/scx_exit() call; warn = WARN_ON*()/BUG_ON(); guard = an if whose branch leaves the normal path (see cond/action); call = call to 'target'

lock.description: Lock class token: rq (struct rq lock, any of raw_spin_rq_lock*, rq_lock*, task_rq_lock), dsq (scx_dispatch_q.lock), pi_lock (task_struct.pi_lock), irqs_disabled (local IRQ state, assertions only), or the lock's variable name for anything else. Which instance is meant is given by expr.

expr.description: Source expression of the object the event acts on, in the scope of this function: the lock instance for lock/unlock/assert_* (e.g. &dsq->lock, dst_rq, task_rq(p)), the target object for atomic/write (e.g. p, this_rq). Lets consumers bind the token to a specific instance.

op.description: lock/unlock: absent for plain (incl. _irq/_irqsave/_nested variants), 'trylock' when the acquisition may fail. atomic: read, read_acquire, set, set_release, cmpxchg, inc, dec, set_bit, clear_bit, test_and_clear_bit. write: set, or, andnot, inc, dec, write_once, list_add, list_del, rb_insert, rb_erase, rcu_assign.

cond.description: guard: the source condition of the if. Other kinds: the event happens only when this source condition holds (e.g. inside an if/else branch).

action.description: guard only: what the branch taken when cond is true does. return = leaves the function; error = scx_error()/WARN, then leaves the function; fallback = replaces a value and continues (e.g. use the global DSQ); continue = skips the rest of a block or loop iteration and continues in the function. Calls made inside a returning branch are listed just before the guard with the same cond.

target.description: Callee for kind=call (a key of nodes, or the ops/method slot of an indirect call)

msg.description: error/warn: the message or WARN condition
